74:1: God Almighty says: O you who are wrapped up in your garments: O you who are wrapped up in your garments when you sleep. It was mentioned that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was told this while he was wrapped in a velvet blanket. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim: O you wrapped up in a blanket. He said: He was wrapped in a blanket. It was mentioned that this verse was the first thing revealed from the Qur’an to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that it was said to him: O you wrapped in your cloak. Yunus told us, saying: Ibn Wahb told us, saying: Yunus told us, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, saying: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman told me, that Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said while speaking about the period of revelation: While I was walking, I heard a voice from the sky. I raised my head and saw the angel who had come to me with courage sitting on a chair between the sky and the earth. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I knelt down in fear of him, and I went to my family and said: Cover me up, cover me up, so they covered me up. Then God revealed: O you wrapped in garments, arise and warn, and glorify your Lord... until His saying: and avoid abomination. He said: Then the revelation continued. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us: Al-Awza’i told us: Yahya bin Abi Katheer told us: I asked Abu Salamah: Which of the Qur’an was revealed first? He said: O you wrapped up in your cloak. I said: They say: Read in the name of your Lord who created (al-Alaq 96:1). Abu Salamah said: I asked Jabir bin Abdullah: Which of the Qur’an was revealed first? He said: O you who are wrapped up in your cloak. I said: “They say: ‘Read in the name of your Lord who created’” (al-Alaq 96:1). He said: “I will not tell you except what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, told us.” He said: “I stayed in Hira’, and when I had finished my stay, I went down and went into the valley. I was called, so I looked to my right and to my left and behind me and in front of me, but I did not see anything. Then I looked above my head and saw Him sitting on a throne between the heaven and the earth. I was afraid of Him, as Uthman ibn Amr said. It is true. So I knelt down before Him and met Khadija. I said: ‘Cover me.’ So they covered me and poured water over me. Then God revealed to me: ‘O you who are wrapped up in your cloak, arise and warn.’” Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki` narrated to us, on the authority of Ali ibn Mubarak, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, who said: I asked Abu Salamah about the first part of the Qur’an to be revealed. He said: O you wrapped up in your cloak was revealed first. He said: I said: They say: Read in the name of your Lord who created (al-Alaq 96:1). He said: I asked Jabir ibn Abdullah, and he said: I will not tell you anything except what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told us. He said: I stayed in Hira’, and when I had finished staying in Hira’ I came down and heard a voice. I looked to my right and did not see anything, and I looked behind me and did not see anything. I raised my head and saw something, so I came to Khadijah and said: Cover me and pour cold water over me. Then O you wrapped up in your cloak was revealed. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, who said: The revelation ceased for a period of time, and he became very sad. He started running to the tops of mountains to throw himself down from them. Whenever he reached the top of a mountain, Gabriel, peace be upon him, would appear to him and say: You are the Prophet of God. He would calm his nerves and his soul would calm down. The Prophet, peace be upon him, used to talk about that. He said: While I was walking one day, I saw the angel who used to come to me at Hira on a throne between the heaven and the earth. I was terrified by him, so I went back to Khadija and said: Cover me. So we covered him, that is, we covered him, and God revealed: “O you wrapped in a cloak, arise and warn. And your Lord glorify. And your garments purify.” Al-Zuhri said: The first thing that was revealed to him was: Read in the name of your Lord who created (al-Alaq 96:1)... until he reached that which he did not know (al-Alaq 96:5). The commentators differed on the meaning of his statement, O you who are wrapped up, and some of them said: The meaning of this is: O you who sleeps in your clothes. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, O you wrapped up in garments, he said: O you who sleep. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, O you who are wrapped up in your garments, meaning: the one wrapped up in his garments. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: O you who are wrapped in prophecy and its burdens. Who said that? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abd Al-A’la told us, he said: Dawud was asked about this verse, O you wrapped up in your garments, so he told us on the authority of Ikrimah that he said: You have wrapped up this matter, so carry it out.
74:2: And His saying: Rise and warn means that God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Rise from your sleep and warn your people who associated partners with God and worshipped other than Him of God’s punishment. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Arise and warn: meaning warn of God’s punishment and its consequences for the nations, and the severity of His vengeance.
74:3: And His saying: And your Lord, so glorify Him. God Almighty says: And your Lord, O Muhammad, so glorify Him by worshipping Him and turning to Him for your needs, rather than any other god or rival.
74:4: And his saying: And your clothing purify. The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: Do not wear your clothing in disobedience, nor in treachery. Mention who said that. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And your clothing purify. He said: Have you not heard the words of Ghailan bin Salamah: Praise be to God, I do not wear the garment of an immoral person, nor do I cover myself with treachery. Abu Kurayb told us: Mus`ab bin Salam told us, on the authority of Al-Ajlah, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A man came to him while I was sitting and said: What do you think of the statement of God, And your garments purify? He said: Do not wear them for disobedience or for treachery. Then he said: Have you not heard the statement of Ghailan bin Salamah Al-Thaqafi: Praise be to God, I do not wear the garment of an immoral person, nor do I cover myself with treachery. Saeed bin Yahya told us: Hafs bin Ghayath told us, on the authority of Al-Ajlah, on the authority of Ikrimah, and his saying, And your garments purify, he said: Do not wear them for treachery or for immorality. Then he recited this poem of Ghailan bin Salamah. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Ajlah bin Abdullah Al-Kindi, on the authority of Ikrimah, And your clothing purify, he said: Do not wear your clothing in disobedience. Have you not heard the words of Ghailan bin Salamah Al-Thaqafi: Praise be to God, I do not wear the garment of an immoral person, nor do I cover myself with treachery. Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told me, he said: Hajjaj told us, Ibn Jurayj said, Ata’ told me, that he heard Ibn Abbas say: And your garments purify. He said: From sin. He said: Purify the garments in the speech of the Arabs. Saeed bin Yahya told us: Hafs bin Ghayath Al-Qadi told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And your clothing purify. He said: In the speech of the Arabs: clean clothing. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim: And your clothing purify He said: From sins. Abu Kuraib told us: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And your clothing purify He said: From sins. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And your clothes purify. He said: It is an Arabic word that the Arabs used to say, Purify your clothes, meaning from sins. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And your garments purify, meaning: purify them from sins. So the Arabs used to call a man who broke his promise and did not fulfill it dirty his garments, and if he fulfilled his promise and repaired it, they said: purified garments. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And your clothing purify He said: From sin. He said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim: And your clothing purify. He said: From sin. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And your clothing purify, that he said: Do not wear your clothing in disobedience. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata`, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And your clothing purify. He said: From sin. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: From sin. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Ajlah, who heard Ikrimah say: Do not wear your clothes while committing a sin. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer and Ata’, who said: Among the sins. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Do not wear clothes made from impure earnings. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And your clothing purify. He said: Do not let the clothing that you wear come from impure earnings. And it is said: Do not wear your clothing in disobedience. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Correct your work. Who said that? Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told me: Fadil bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And your clothing purify, he said: Your work, so improve it. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin, regarding his statement, And your clothing, purify, he said: Your work, so improve it. And if a man’s work was bad, they would say: So-and-so has bad clothing. And if his work was good, they would say: So-and-so has clean clothing. Others said about this: Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, And your clothing purify: I am neither a soothsayer nor a magician, so ignore what they said. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Wash it with water and purify it from impurity. Who said that? Abbas bin Abi Talib told me, he said: Ali bin Abdullah bin Jaafar told us, on the authority of Ahmad bin Musa bin Abi Maryam, the owner of Al-Lulu, he said: Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, And your garments purify, he said: Wash them with water. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And your garments purify, he said: The polytheists did not purify themselves, so He ordered him to purify himself and to purify his garments. This statement, which was made by Ibn Sirin and Ibn Zayd, is the most obvious meaning of it. What was said by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and Ibn Zakariya is a statement that most of the predecessors agreed upon, that he meant by it: your body, so purify it from sins. And God knows best what he meant by that.
74:5: And abandon the abomination. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. Some of the reciters of Medina and most of the reciters of Kufa recited it: And the abomination with a kasra on the ra', and some of the Meccans and Medinans recited it: And the abomination with a damma on the ra'. Those who recited the ra' with a damma directed it to the idols and said: The meaning of the statement is: And abandon the worship of the idols and leave their service. Those who recited the ra' with a kasra directed it to the torment and said: Its meaning is: And abandon the torment, meaning abandon whatever deeds cause you to be tormented. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings, so whichever one the reader recites is correct. The damma and kasra in this are two dialects with one meaning, and we did not find any of the early scholars of interpretation who differentiated between the interpretations of this. Rather, as far as we have been informed, the only difference between them was Al-Kisa’i. The commentators differed on the meaning of rajz in this context. Some of them said: It refers to idols. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Avoid abomination, he said: Anger, which is idols. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And avoid all abomination, he said: idols. Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Waki` told us, on the authority of Isra`il, he said: Abu Ja`far: I stopped it, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid and Ikrimah, And avoid abomination, he said: idols. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And avoid abomination, meaning Isaf and Na’ila, and they were two idols that were near the House, and whoever came upon them would wipe their faces. So God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to avoid them and keep away from them. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri: And avoid abominations. He said: They are idols. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And avoid all abomination, he said: The abomination is their gods that they used to worship. He ordered him to avoid them, so he would not come to them or come near them. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Avoid disobedience and sin. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim: And avoid abomination, meaning sin. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And avoid sin, he said: Avoid sin. We have already explained the meaning of sin previously with evidence that suffices from repeating it in this context.
74:6: And His saying, And do not bestow a favor, expecting more in return. The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: And do not give, O Muhammad, a gift, expecting more in return. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And do not bestow a favor, seeking a greater reward in return, he said: Do not give a gift seeking something better in return. Abu Hamid Al-Himsi Ahmad bin Al-Mughira told us: Abu Haywa Shureih bin Yazid Al-Hadrami told us: Artah told us on the authority of Damr bin Habib and Abu Al-Ahwas regarding his statement, And do not bestow a favor, expecting more in return, he said: Do not give something, expecting more in return. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us: Someone who heard `Ikrimah say: And do not bestow a favor expecting more in return. He said: Do not give a gift expecting to receive more in return. Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told me: Fadil told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Ibrahim: And do not bestow favors, expecting more in return. He said: Do not give in order to receive more in return. Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Asim told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding His statement, And do not bestow a favor, expecting more in return, he said: Do not give something in order to take more in return. Abu Kuraib narrated that Wakee’ narrated to us, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: And do not bestow a favor expecting more in return. He said: Do not give in order to receive more in return. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement, And do not bestow a favor, expecting more in return, he said: Do not give in order to be given more in return. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement, And do not bestow favors, expecting more in return, he said: Do not give something in order to increase it. Abu Kuraib told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Rawad, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: It is lawful usury, and it was specifically for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Abu Hujairah, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: There are two types of usury: lawful and unlawful. As for the lawful, it is gifts, and the unlawful is usury. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And do not bestow favors, expecting more in return, meaning: Do not give anything, for you will only be rewarded for this world and its rivals. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And do not bestow a favor, expecting more in return. He said: Do not give something in order to be rewarded with something better than it. Tawus also said this. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And do not bestow favor, expecting more in return, he said: You give money as a favor, hoping for a better reward in this world. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Do not give in order to be given more than that. He said: Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Ibrahim, And do not bestow favors expecting more in return. He said: Do not give in order to increase your reward. He said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim, And do not bestow a favor, expecting more in return. He said: It is specifically for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and for people in general, who are given more. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Do not bestow your deeds upon your Lord, hoping for more. Who said that? Mujahid bin Musa told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sufyan bin Hussein told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, And do not bestow a favor, expecting more in return, he said: Do not bestow a favor on your deeds, expecting more in return from your Lord. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Hudha told us, he said: Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And do not bestow favors, expecting a greater reward in return. He said: Do not bestow favors, expecting a greater reward in return. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Yunus bin Nafi’ Abu Ghanim told us, on the authority of Abu Sahl Katheer bin Ziyad, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And do not bestow favors, expecting more in return. He said: Do not bestow favors, expecting more in return for your good deeds. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi` bin Anas, And do not bestow favors, expecting more in return. He said: Do not let your deeds be considered many in your eyes, for what God has bestowed upon you and given you is little. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Do not be weak in seeking more good, and they interpreted the meaning of his statement and do not be ungrateful as meaning do not be weak, from their saying: a weak rope: if it is weak. Who said that? Abu Hamid bin Al-Mughirah Al-Himsi told us: Abdullah bin Omar told us: Muhammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And do not bestow favors, expecting more in return, he said: Do not be too weak to expect more in goodness. He said: To bestow favors in Arabic means to be weak. Others said about this: Do not bestow prophethood upon people and take a reward from them for it. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And do not bestow favors, hoping to get more in return, he said: Do not bestow favors of prophethood and the Qur’an with which We sent you, hoping to get more in return, taking a worldly reward in exchange for it. The first of these sayings that is most correct in my opinion is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of that is: Do not be a favor to your Lord by increasing your good deeds. I said that this is more correct, because it is in the context of verses in which God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to be diligent in calling to Him and to be patient with the harm he encountered in it. So this is more likely to be of the types of those than it is of the others. It was mentioned on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud that this is in his recitation And do not bestow a favor, expecting more in return.
74:7: And His saying: And for the sake of your Lord, be patient. God Almighty says: And for the sake of your Lord, be patient with whatever hardship you encounter therein. A group of interpreters said something similar to what we said about this, with differences among the interpreters. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And for the sake of your Lord, be patient, he said: with what you have been given. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And for the sake of your Lord, be patient, he said: He carried a great matter, fighting the Arabs, then the non-Arabs after the Arabs for the sake of God. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: For the sake of your Lord, be patient with what He gives you. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim: And for the sake of your Lord be patient. He said: Be patient with what He gives you. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Be patient with what God gives you. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding His statement, And for the sake of your Lord, be patient, he said: I have given you, be patient with it.
74:8: He, the Most High, means by His saying: Then when the Trumpet is blown, that will be a severe day. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Kurayb narrated: Ibn Fadil and Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Atiyyah al-Awfi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, And when the trumpet is blown, that will be a difficult Day, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘How can I enjoy myself while the companion of the trumpet has taken hold of the trumpet and bent his forehead, listening for the command to blow it?’ The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘What should we say?’ He said, ‘You should say, “God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. In God we trust.”’” Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Abu Raja’ told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, Then when the trumpet is blown, he said: When the trumpet is blown. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Abu Al-Nu’man Al-Hakam bin Abdullah told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, Then when the trumpet is blown, something similar. Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid: Then when the trumpet is blown. He said: When the trumpet is blown. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Then when the trumpet is blown, he said: on the trumpet. He said: It is something like a trumpet. Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And when the trumpet is blown, he said: It is the day when the trumpet will be blown. Ibn Abbas said: "The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to his companions and said: How can I be at ease while the companion of the horn has taken hold of the trumpet, and he bent his forehead and then turned his ear to hear when the blast would be ordered? This was very difficult for his companions, so he ordered them to say: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. In God we trust." Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Then when the trumpet is blown, meaning: the trumpet. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said: Al-Hasan said: Then when the trumpet is blown: He said: When the trumpet is blown. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And when the trumpet is blown, and the trumpet means the trumpets, and the trumpets means creation. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say, regarding His statement, Then when the trumpet is blown, meaning: the trumpet. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, regarding his statement, Then when the trumpet is blown, he said: The trumpet is the trumpet. Mahran told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, the same. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Then when the trumpet is blown, he said: The trumpet. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
74:9: Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Then that Day will be a difficult Day, meaning: severe. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qanadah, God Almighty said: That will be a difficult day, so God made clear to whom it will fall.
74:10: It is not easy for the unbelievers.
74:11: And His saying: Leave Me and he whom I created alone, the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Eat, O Muhammad, the matter of the one whom I created alone in his mother’s womb, who has no wealth or children except me. He mentioned that he meant by that: Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah Al-Makhzumi. Who said that? Sufyan told us, he said: Waki` told us, he said: Yunus bin Bakir told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zayd, on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr or `Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, he said: God revealed concerning Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira His saying: Leave Me and he whom I created alone and His saying: By your Lord, We will surely question them all (al-Hijr 15:92)... to the end. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Leave Me and he whom I created alone, he said: I created him alone, with no wealth or children. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sharik, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Leave Me and he whom I created alone. He said: It was revealed about Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira, and so it is for all of creation. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Leave Me and he whom I created alone, that is, Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira. God brought him forth from his mother’s womb alone, with no money or children, so God provided him with money and children, wealth and growth. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Leave Me and he whom I created alone... to His statement, This is nothing but magic passed on... until he reached, I will cast him into Hellfire. He said: This verse was revealed about Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Leave Me and he whom I created alone, meaning Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira.
74:12: And I gave him abundant wealth. The interpreters of the Qur’an differed regarding this money that God mentioned, and stated that He had given it to the newborn. What was it and what was its amount? Some of them said: It was dinars, and its amount was one thousand dinars. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Ismail bin Ibrahim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Mujahid: And I gave him abundant wealth. He said: His wealth was a thousand dinars. Saleh bin Mismar Al-Marwazi told us, he said: Al-Harith bin Imran Al-Kufi told us, he said: Muhammad bin Suqa told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement, And I gave him abundant wealth, he said: A thousand dinars. Others said: His wealth was four thousand dinars. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, And I gave him abundant wealth. He said: I was informed that it was four thousand dinars. Others said: His property was land. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Wahb bin Jarir told me, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Salim, regarding His statement, And I have given him abundant wealth, he said: The land. Ahmad bin Ishaq Al-Ahwazi told us: Wahb bin Jarir told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Salim, similarly. Others said: It was the yield of each month. Who said that? Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told us: Halbas, the imam of Ibn Ulayyah Mosque, told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Umar, may God be pleased with him, regarding his statement, And I have given him abundant wealth, he said: The yield of one month after another. Abu Hafs Al-Hiri told me: Halbas Al-Dab’i told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, similarly, but he did not say on the authority of Umar. Ahmad bin Al-Walid Al-Ramli told us: Ghalib bin Halbas told us: My father told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, similarly, and he did not say on the authority of Umar. Ahmad bin Al-Walid told us: Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us: Halbas bin Muhammad Al-Ajli told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Umar, similarly. The correct thing to say about this is as God said: And I gave him abundant wealth, which is abundant and extended in number or area.
74:13: God Almighty says: And He made for him sons as witnesses. He mentioned that they were ten. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Ibrahim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Mujahid: And sons as witnesses. He said: His sons were ten.
74:14: And His saying: And I made life easy for him. God Almighty says: And I made life easy for him. As Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, And I prepared a way for him. He said: He spread it out for him. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And I prepared for him a preparation, he said: of money and children.
74:15: And His statement: Then he hopes that I will give him more, God Almighty says: Then he hopes and expects that I will give him more money and children than I have given him.
74:16: No, he says: That is not as he hopes and hopes that I will increase his wealth and children, and prepare him in this world. Indeed, he was stubborn towards Our signs. He says: Indeed, this one whom I created alone was stubborn towards Our signs, which are God's proofs to His creation from the books and messengers, meaning he was obstinate towards the truth and turned away from it, like a stubborn camel. From this is the saying of the one who said: If you come down, make me the middle one, for I am old and cannot bear to be stubborn. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Indeed, he was stubborn towards Our signs, he said: He denied. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Indeed, he was obstinate toward Our signs. Muhammad ibn Amr said: Obstinate toward them, and Al-Harith said: Obstinate toward them, avoiding them. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, obstinately, he said: opposing the truth and deviating from it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Indeed, he was stubborn towards Our signs, ungrateful to the signs of God, rejecting them. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, Opposing Our signs. He said: Struggling. It was also said: Obstinate. It is from ‘anadah obstinacy, so it is mu’addid, just as it was said: Next year, but it is actually next year.
74:17: And His saying: I will make him climb uphill, God Almighty says: I will burden him with a difficult and painful torment from which he will have no relief. It was said: The ascent is a mountain in Hell that the people of Hell are required to climb. The narration mentioned that: Muhammad ibn Amara al-Asadi told me: Muhammad ibn Saeed ibn Zaydah told us: Sharik told us, on the authority of Amara, on the authority of Atiyyah, on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: I will make him ascend it. He said: It is a mountain of fire in Hell. They will be made to climb it. When he places his hands down, it melts. When he raises them up, it returns. When he places his foot down, it does the same. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Amr ibn al-Harith told me, on the authority of Diraj, on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: ‘The Ascent is a mountain of fire, one ascends it for seventy autumns, then falls from it like that forever.’” Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, I will make him ascend with difficulty. He said: A difficult form of torment. Al-Harith told me, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, I will make him ascend with a painful ascent, meaning: a torment from which there is no relief. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Sulayman told us, he said: Abu Hilal told us, on the authority of Qatada, I will make him ascend with difficulty. He said: A difficult form of torment. Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, I will make him ascend with difficulty, he said: tired from the torment.
74:18: God Almighty says: This one whom You created alone, thought about what He revealed to His servant Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the Qur’an, and considered what He says in it.
74:19: He killed as he decreed. He says: Then he cursed as he decreed the one who descended upon it.
74:20: God Almighty said: Then he killed, as He decreed.
74:21: Then he looked He says: Then he narrated about that.
74:22: Then he frowned meaning: then he closed his eyes. And he frowned meaning: his face turned dark. From this is the saying of Tobah bin Al-Humayr: I was disturbed by her aversion and her turning away from my needs and her stubbornness. The people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that, and the report came from Al-Wahid that he did it. The narration mentioned that: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ubadah ibn Mansur, on the authority of Ikrimah, that al-Walid ibn al-Mughira came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and recited the Qur’an to him, and it was as if he felt pity for him. When this reached Abu Jahl, he said: O uncle, your people want to collect wealth for you. He said: Why not? He said: They will give it to you, for you came to Muhammad, exposing yourself to what came before him. He said: The Quraysh know that I am the wealthiest of them. He said: Then say something about him that will make your people know that you will deny what he said and that you hate it. He said: “What should I say about him? By God, there is no man among you who knows more poetry than me, nor more knowledgeable about its rajaz than me, nor about its qasida, nor about the poetry of the jinn, and by God, your people will not be pleased until you say something about him.” He said: Then leave me until I think about it. When he thought about it, he said: This is magic that he has influenced from someone else. Then the verse was revealed: Leave me and he whom I created alone. Qatadah said: He came out of his mother’s womb alone. Then this verse was revealed until he reached nineteen.”. Muhammad bin Saeed told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Indeed, he thought and considered… to Then he frowned and frowned. He said: Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah entered upon Abu Bakr bin Abi Quhafah, may God be pleased with him, asking him about the Qur’an. When he told him, he went out to the Quraysh and said, “How strange is what Ibn Abi Kabshah says. By God, it is neither poetry, nor magic, nor madness, and his words are the words of God.” When the group of Quraysh heard that, they consulted and said, By God, if Al-Walid converts to Islam, the Quraysh will convert to Islam. When Abu Ja’al heard that, he said, By God, I will take care of his affairs for you. He went until he entered his house and said to Al-Walid, Didn’t you see that your people have collected the alms for you? He said, Are you not the richest of them in wealth and children? Abu Jahl said to him, They say that you only go to Ibn Abi Quhafah to take some of his food. Al-Walid said, “My clan has spoken of it, so he should not fall short of the rest of the Banu Qusayy. I am not close to Abu Neither Bakr, nor Omar, nor Ibn Abi Kabsha, and his words were nothing but magic that was being practiced. So God revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Leave Me and he whom I created alone”... to Leave nothing behind or spare anything. Bishr told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, He thought and planned, they claimed that he said: By God, I looked at what this man said, and I saw that he had no hair, although he had sweetness, and he had a fresh complexion, and he was rising and rising, and I have no doubt that it was magic. So God revealed about him, Then he killed, how he planned, and the verse, Then he frowned and frowned, meaning he closed the space between his eyes and frowned. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, Think and consider, he said: Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah on the day of Dar Al-Nadwa. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Leave Me and he whom I created alone, meaning Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called him to Islam, and said: Let me look, so he thought. Then he looked, then he frowned and frowned, then he turned away and was arrogant, and said, ‘This is not but magic passed on.’ So God ordained Hell for him. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, Leave Me and he whom I created alone * And for whom I have given abundant wealth... to His statement, This is nothing but magic that is passed on, he said: This is Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira. He said: I will cut off this man for you tonight. So he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and found him standing praying and reciting the Quran. He came to them and they said: What is it? He said: I heard a sweet, green, fruitful saying that captures hearts. They said: It is poetry. He said: No, by God, it is not poetry. No one knows more about poetry than me. Didn’t the poets Nabigha, so-and-so, and so-and-so present to me their poetry? They said: He is a soothsayer. He said: No, by God, he is not a soothsayer. Divination was presented to me. They said: This is the magic of the ancients that he wrote down. He said: I do not know if it is anything, so perhaps it is magic that is passed on. So he recited, Then he was killed how he decreed * Then he was killed how he decreed. He said: He was killed how he decreed when he said: It is not poetry. Then he was killed how he decreed when he said: It is not soothsaying.
74:23: And His statement: Then he turned away and was arrogant. God Almighty says: Then he turned away from believing and confirming what God revealed of His Book, and was arrogant about acknowledging the truth.
74:24: God Almighty said: He said, ‘This is nothing but magic that has been passed on to him.’ He said: He has passed it on to someone else. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail bin Sami’, on the authority of Abu Razin: This is nothing but magic that has been passed on. He said: He takes it from someone else. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Razin: This is nothing but magic that has been passed on. He said: He has passed it on to someone else.
74:25: And His saying: This is nothing but the word of a human being, God Almighty says, informing about what was said by the only one in the Qur’an: This is nothing but the word of a human being. What Muhammad is reciting is nothing but the word of a human being. He says: It is nothing but the word of the son of Adam, and it is not the word of God.
74:26: God Almighty means by His saying, I will cast him into Hellfire, that He will send him to a gate of Hellfire called Saqar. Saqar was not used in the genitive case because it is one of the names of Hellfire.
74:27: God Almighty says: And what will make you know what Hellfire is? God Almighty says: And what will make you know, O Muhammad, what Hellfire is? Then God Almighty explained what Hellfire is, saying: It is fire.
74:28: God Almighty says: It does not leave anyone alive in it, nor does it spare anyone dead in it, but rather it burns them every time it recreates them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, It does not leave anything behind and does not spare anything, he said: It does not cause death and does not give life. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told me: Ubaidullah bin Musa told us: Abu Laila told us, on the authority of Marthad, regarding his statement, It does not leave anything behind or spare them, he said: It does not leave anything behind that it may eat them, and when they are created for it, it does not spare them until it takes them and consumes them.
74:29: And His saying: A scourge for mankind means that He, may His praise be glorified, is a scourge for the mankind of its people. The scourge is from the curse of Saqar, and by responding to it it is raised, and the raising is good in it, and it is indefinite, and Saqar is definite, because of what it contains of the meaning of praise. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, A light for mankind, he said: the skin. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Razin, A light for the people, he said: It scorches the skin with a scorching heat, leaving it blacker than night. Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakim told me: My father and Shuaib bin Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Khalid bin Yazid, on the authority of Abu Hilal, who said: Zaid bin Aslam said: A glare for humanity means their bodies will shine upon it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, a burning for mankind means a burning of the skin. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, A scourge for mankind meaning: It burns the human skin. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, a glare for humanity, he said: It changes humanity, it burns humanity. It is said: He was glared at by his facing the sky. Then he said: The fire changes their colors. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail bin Sami’, on the authority of Abu Razin: A scourge for mankind changed their skins and made them black. Abu Kuraib told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Sami’, on the authority of Abu Razin, similarly. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, a scorch for mankind, meaning the skin of man, that he said: it burns his skin. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this matter: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, a spectacle for mankind, he said: exposed. I fear that this report of Ali ibn Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, is a mistake, and that the place of exposed is changed, but a misprint was made in it.
74:30: And His saying: Nineteen over it means that God Almighty says: Over Saqar are nineteen of the guards. It was mentioned that when this was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Abu Jahl said: “Muhammad ibn Sa`d narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas: ‘Nineteen over them’… to His saying: ‘And those who believe will increase in faith.’ When Abu Jahl heard that, he said to the Quraysh 106:‘May your mothers be bereaved of you! I hear Ibn Abi Kabsha telling you that the keepers of Hell are nineteen and you are the dark ones. Are ten of you unable to strike a man from the keepers of Hell?’ So it was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to go to Abu Jahl, take him by the hand in the plain of Mecca and say to him: ‘It is better for you, then it is better, then it is better for you, then it is better’ (Al-Qiyamah 22:34-35). When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did that to him, Abu Jahl said: ‘By God, you and your Lord will not do anything.’ So God disgraced him on the day of Badr.” Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, There are nineteen over it. It was mentioned to us that when this verse was revealed, Abu Jahl said: O people of Quraysh, how can ten of you overcome one of the keepers of Hellfire, when you are the darkest? So your companion tells you that there are nineteen over it. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Abu Jahl said: Muhammad tells you that the keepers of Hell are nineteen and you are the dark ones, so that ten may gather against one. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd, in his statement, Nineteen over it, he said: Its treasurers are nineteen.
74:31: And His statement: And We have not made the keepers of the Fire except angels. God Almighty says: And We have not made the keepers of the Fire except angels. He says to Abu Jahl in his statement to the Quraysh 106:Is it not possible for every ten of you to defeat one of them? So who can defeat the keepers of the Fire, who are the angels? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And We have not made the companions of the Fire except angels, he said: We did not make them men, so that each man takes a man as this one said. And His saying: And We did not make their number except as a trial for those who disbelieved. He says: And We did not make the number of these guards except as a trial for those who disbelieved in God from the polytheists of Quraysh. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And We did not make their number except as a trial for those who disbelieved: except as a trial. God made the report about several trials for those who disbelieved, because of their denial of that, and some of them saying to their companions: I will suffice you against them. Mention the report about who said that: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, nineteen, he said: They were made a trial. Abu Al-Ashd ibn Al-Jumahi said: They will not reach my level until I abort them from Hell. And His statement: So that those who were given the Scripture may be certain, God Almighty says: So that the people of the Torah and the Gospel may be certain of the truth of what is in their books about the number of guards of Hell, since that is in accordance with what God revealed in His Book to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, That those who were given the Scripture may be certain and those who believe may increase in faith, he said: And it is nineteen in the Torah and the Gospel, so God wanted the People of the Scripture to be certain and those who believe to increase in faith. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, That those who were given the Scripture may be certain, he said: They will find it written with them, a number of the keepers of the people of Hell. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, So that those who were given the Scripture may be certain, the Qur’an confirms the books that came before it, all of them, the Torah and the Gospel, that the guardians of Hell are nineteen. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, So that those who were given the Scripture may be certain, he said: So that the People of the Scripture may be certain when the number of the keepers of Hellfire coincides with what is in their books. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, That those who were given the Scripture may be certain, that he said: The number of the guards of Hell is nineteen in the Torah and the Gospel. Ibn Zayd used to say about this: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, So that those who were given the Scripture may be certain, that you are the Messenger of God. And His statement, And those who believe will increase in faith, God Almighty says, And those who believe in God will increase in belief in God and His Messenger by believing in the number of the keepers of Hell. And His statement: And let not those who were given the Scripture and the believers doubt means: The people of the Torah and the Gospel do not doubt the truth of that, nor do the believers in God from the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And His statement: And let those in whose hearts is disease and the disbelievers say, God Almighty says: And let those in whose hearts is disease of hypocrisy and the disbelievers in God from the polytheists of Quraysh say, What did God intend by this example? As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And let those in whose hearts is disease say, meaning hypocrisy. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And that those in whose hearts is disease and the disbelievers may say, ‘What does God intend by this as an example?’ He said: So that He may frighten us with these nineteen. And His statement: Thus does God misguide whom He wills and guides whom He wills, the Most High says: Just as God misguides these hypocrites and polytheists who say about God’s report about the number of the keepers of Hell: What did God intend by this report as an example so that He might frighten us by mentioning their number, and the believers might be guided by it, so that by believing them they might increase in faith to their belief? Thus does God misguide whom He wills of His creation so He lets him down from attaining the truth and guides whom He wills of them, so He grants him success in attaining the correct path. And none knows the soldiers of your Lord because of their great number except Him: meaning God. As Bishr told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him, meaning their great number. And His saying: And it is only a reminder to mankind, God Almighty says: And the fire that I described is only a reminder with which mankind, namely the children of Adam, is reminded. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And it is only a reminder to mankind, meaning the Fire. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And it is only a reminder to mankind, he said: the Fire.
74:32: God Almighty means by His saying, No, that the statement is not as those who claim that it is sufficient for his polytheist companions, the guardians of Hell, to abort them from it, then our Lord Almighty swore and said, By the moon * And by the night when it departs, meaning: And by the night when it turns away, going away. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
74:33: Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the night when it departs: when it turns away. Others said about this: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the night when it departs. Its departure: its darkness. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra recited it as when he turned away, and some of the reciters of Mecca and Kufa recited it as when he turned away. The correct thing to say about this, in our view, is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. Scholars of Arabic speech differed on this. Some of the Kufians said: They are two dialects. It is said: dabar al-nahar wa adbara, dabar al-sif wa adbara. He said: And so are qabal and aqbal. So if they say: aqbal al-rakib wa aqbal, they do not say it except with an alif. Some Basrans said: And the night when it departs meaning: when the day departs and is at its end. He said: And it is said: dabarni: if he came behind me, and adbara: if he turned away. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two languages with the same meaning. This is because it is reported from the Arabs: May God make ugly what is before Him and what is behind Him. Another is that the people of interpretation did not distinguish between the two readings in their interpretation, and this is evidence that they did so as well, because they have the same meaning.
74:34: And His saying: And the morning when it dawns God Almighty says: And the morning when it shines. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the morning when it brightens when it shines and approaches.
74:35: It is one of the greatest things. God Almighty says: Hell is one of the greatest things, meaning the great things. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told me, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Indeed, it is one of the greatest, meaning: Hell. Abu Al-Sa’ib told us: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Sami’, on the authority of Abu Razin: It is one of the greatest. He said: Hell. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, Indeed, it is one of the greatest, he said: This is the Fire. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: It is one of the greatest sins. He said: It is the Fire. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Indeed, it is one of the greatest, meaning: Hell. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, It is one of the greatest, meaning: Hell.
74:36: And His saying: A warner to mankind, God Almighty says: The Fire is one of the greatest, a warner to the children of Adam. The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of his statement: A warner to mankind, and what is described by that. Some of them said: He meant the fire. They said: It is an attribute of the ha’ in his statement: It is. They said: It is the warner. So according to what these people say, the warner is in the accusative case as a break from one of the major things, because one of the major things is definite, and his statement: A warner is indefinite, and the speech might be better to stop at it without it. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Al-Hasan said: By God, I have not warned people of anything more terrible than it, or a calamity more terrible than it. Others said: Rather, this is from the attribute of God Almighty, and it is report from God about Himself, that He is a warner to His creation. According to this statement, the accusative of His statement, a warner, must be to be taken as a departure from the previous statement, so the meaning of the statement is: And We have not made the companions of the Fire except angels as warners to mankind, meaning: a warning to them. So His statement, a warner, means a warning to them, just as He said, How then was a warner? meaning My warning. And it can also mean: It is one of the greatest things, so We made that a warner. So His statement, It is one of the greatest things, conveys the meaning of We made that thus, and this meaning is what was intended by the one who said that, God willing. Who said that? Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Razin, Indeed, it is one of the greatest things. He said: Hell. A warner to mankind. God says: I am a warner to you from it, so fear it. Others said: Rather, this is a description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They said: The subject of the word warner is in the accusative case as a state of what is in his saying: Rise up. They said: The meaning of the statement is: Rise up as a warner to humanity, so warn. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, A warner to mankind, he said: Creation. He said: The children of Adam, mankind. So it was said to him, Muhammad the warner. He said: Yes, he warns them.
74:37: And His statement: For whoever among you wishes to advance or to hold back, God Almighty says: A warner to mankind for whoever among you wishes, O people, to advance in obeying God, or hold back in disobeying God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: For whoever among you wills to advance or to fall behind, he said: Whoever wills may follow the obedience of God, and whoever wills may fall behind from it. Bishr told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: For whoever among you wishes to advance or hold back: advance in obeying God, or hold back in disobeying Him.
74:38: God Almighty says: Every soul is commanded and forbidden for what it did of disobedience to God in this world, and is held hostage in Hell, except the companions of the right, for they are not held hostage, but they will be in gardens questioning one another about the criminals. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Every soul will be held in pledge for what it has earned. He said: It will be held accountable for its deeds. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Every soul is a pledge for what it has earned, except the companions of the right hand. He said: All people are locked up except the companions of the right hand. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Every soul will be held in pledge for what it has earned, except the companions of the right hand, he said: They will not be held accountable. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, Every soul is a pledge for what it has earned, except the companions of the right, the companions of the right are not held in pledge for their sins, but God forgives them. And he recited the statement of God, Except the chosen servants of God (37:40, 74, 128, 210), he said: God will not hold them accountable for their evil deeds, but God will forgive them and overlook their faults as He promised them. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Every soul will be held in pledge for what it has earned, that he said: Every soul for whom the word of punishment has been previously given, God will hold it in pledge in the Fire. God will not hold in pledge anyone from the people of Paradise. Have you not heard that He said, Every soul will be held in pledge for what it has earned, except the companions of the right hand, that is, they will not be held in pledge. In gardens questioning one another. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, Except the companions of the right hand, he said: If one of them has been given the word of punishment, his home in Hell will be a pledge in it, and none of the people of Paradise will be a pledge in Paradise, asking one another about it. The commentators differed regarding the companions of the right hand whom God mentioned in this passage. Some of them said: They are the children of Muslims. Who said that? Wasil bin Abdul A’la told me: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Uthman, on the authority of Zadan, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, regarding this verse: Every soul is a pledge for what it has earned, except the companions of the right hand. He said: They are the children. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Muammil told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Uthman Abu Al-Yaqzan, on the authority of Zadan Abu Omar, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, regarding his statement, Every soul is a pledge for what it has earned, except the companions of the right hand, he said: They are the children of the Muslims.
74:39: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Uthman ibn Umair Abu Al-Yaqzan, on the authority of Zadan, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, regarding his statement: Except the companions of the right hand, he said: The children of the Muslims. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu al-Yaqzan, on the authority of Zadan, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him: Except the companions of the right hand. He said: They are the children. Others said: They are the angels. Who said that? Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki` narrated to us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Al-A`mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They are the angels. Whoever said: The companions of the right hand in this place mean the children and infants of the Muslims. Whoever said: They are the angels, because these people did not commit sins, and they said: They would not have asked the criminals, What brought you into Hellfire? except that they did not commit sins in this world. If they had committed them and known about them, they would not have asked them about what brought them into Hellfire, because everyone who entered from the children of Adam who has reached the age of accountability and is bound by the obligation of command and prohibition, knows that no one is punished except for disobedience.
74:40: And His saying: In gardens, they will question one another. The companions of the right will say, “In gardens, they will question one another about the criminals who entered Hellfire. What caused you to enter Hellfire?”
74:41: God Almighty says: About the criminals.
74:42: God Almighty says: What has brought you into Hellfire?
74:43: They said, 'We were not among those who prayed.' He says: The criminals said to them: We were not among those who prayed to God in this world.
74:44: God Almighty says: And we did not feed the poor out of miserliness with what God had given them, and to prevent him from his right.
74:45: God Almighty says: And we used to engage in vain talk with those who engage in vain talk. He says: We used to engage in falsehood and in what God hates with those who engage in it. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And we used to engage in idle talk with those who engaged in idle talk. He said: Whenever someone went astray, others went astray with him. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And we used to engage in idle talk with those who engaged in idle talk, he said: They said: Whenever he went astray, we went astray with him.
74:46: And His statement: And we used to deny the Day of Judgment, God Almighty says: They said: And we used to deny the Day of Recompense, Reward, and Punishment, and we did not believe in reward, punishment, or reckoning.
74:47: God Almighty says: Until the certainty comes to us. He says: They said: Until the certainty of death comes to us.
74:48: God Almighty says: So the intercession of intercessors will not benefit them. He says: So those whom God has interceded for on behalf of the sinners among the people of monotheism will not intercede for them, so that their intercession will not benefit them. This is clear evidence that God Almighty mentioned that some of His creation intercedes for others. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl, who said: Abu al-Zura’ told us, on the authority of Abdullah, in a story he mentioned about intercession, he said: Then the angels, the prophets, the martyrs, the righteous, and the believers will intercede, and God will intercede for them and say: I am the Most Merciful of the merciful. So more people will be taken out of the Fire than all of creation was taken out of the Fire, then He will say: I am the Most Merciful of the merciful. Then Abdullah recited: O disbelievers! What has brought you into Hellfire? They will say: We were not of those who prayed, nor did we feed the poor, nor did we engage in idle talk with those who engaged in idle talk, nor did we deny the Day of Judgment. And he made four signs with his hand, then he said: Do you see any good in these people? No one in whom there is good will be left in it. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard my uncle and Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhail, on the authority of Abu Al-Zura’a, who said: Abdullah said: Only four will remain in Hell, or the one with the four the doubt is from Abu Ja’far Al-Tabari, then he recites: What has brought you into Hellfire? They will say: We were not of those who prayed, nor did we feed the poor, and we used to converse with the conversants, and we used to deny the Day of Judgment. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: What benefit will the intercession of intercessors bring to them? You know that God will intercede for the believers on the Day of Resurrection. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: There is a man from my nation through whose intercession God will admit more people into Paradise than the Banu Tamim. Al-Hasan said, more than Rabi’ah and Mudar. We used to say that a martyr intercedes for seventy of his family members. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Then the intercession of intercessors will not benefit them. He said: They know that God intercedes for some of them for others. He said: Abu Thaur told us, Muammar said: And I was told by someone who heard Anas bin Malik say: A man may intercede for two men, three men, or one man. He said: Abu Thaur narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, who said: God will admit into Paradise through the intercession of a man from this nation the likes of Banu Tamim, or he said: more than Banu Tamim, and Al-Hasan said: the likes of Rabi’ah and Mudar.
74:49: And His statement: Why then do they turn away from the reminder? He says: Why do these polytheists turn away from God’s reminder to them through this Qur’an, and do not listen to it and learn a lesson and take heed. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Why then do they turn away from the reminder? That is, from this Qur’an.
74:50: God Almighty says: Why then do these polytheists turn away from the reminder, turning away from it like frightened donkeys fleeing from a lion? The reciters differed in their reading of his statement: mustanfira. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it with a kasra on the fa’, and in the reading of some of the Meccans it also means faring. The correct thing to say about this, according to us, is that they are two well-known readings, with correct meanings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. Al-Farra’ used to say: The fat-ha and kasra in this are common in the speech of the Arabs, and he recited: Hold your donkey, it is on alert after the red beasts that have gone west
74:51: And his saying: She fled from a lion. The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of lion. Some of them said: They are the archers. Who said that? Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Hafs bin Ghayath told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Fleeed from a lion, he said: The archers. Ibn Hamid told me, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, and Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Abu Musa, She fled from a lion, he said: the archers. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: She fled from a lion. He said: They are the archers. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Abu Kuraib told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Qasura he said: A group of snipers from the archers. Al-Harith added in his hadith, he said: Some of them said about Qasura: It is the lion, and some of them: The archers. Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding the statement, fleeing from a lion, he said: Qasoora means archers.
